gate1_baseline.virtual_after_definition: accepted allocator envelope rows excluding weak_or_narrow_market_support bucket

gate2_dependency_surface.target_price_note: target_price is absent from accepted allocator paper trades and is not a dependency of this readout; entry_date and exit prices are validated per window.

gate4.acceptance_rule: Observed-only virtual gate requires aggregate EV/PnL improvement versus the accepted allocator envelope, no canonical-window EV/PnL regression, weak-breadth sample >= 8, virtual-after trades >= 20, survival >= 5%, and no production behavior change. Passing this gate would only justify a later shared default-off helper; it is not retained.

hypothesis: Accepted allocator rows may be tail-risk candidates when signal-date market participation is weak or narrow. Removing that fixed bucket virtually should improve the accepted allocator envelope if the bucket contains crowded continuation decay rather than alpha.

post_run_reflection.forbidden_near_neighbor_retry: Do not sweep breadth fractions, SMA lookbacks, SPY/QQQ cutoffs, allocator source ranks, top-N, notional, hold days, cooldown, or the execution envelope on these frozen windows.
post_run_reflection.new_evidence_required: A retry needs materially new tail-state evidence such as forward closed replacement rows, same-day displacement type, or a PIT flow field beyond OHLCV breadth.
post_run_reflection.why_result_happened: The market-breadth tail bucket did not cleanly separate accepted allocator losers from winners. Failure reasons: window_ev_regression:late_strong, window_pnl_regression:late_strong, window_ev_regression:mid_weak, window_pnl_regression:mid_weak, window_ev_regression:old_thin, window_pnl_regression:old_thin, aggregate_ev_not_improved, aggregate_pnl_not_improved. The accepted allocator already mixes event, revision, volatility, relation, and industry-flow sources; broad breadth can remove valid relief/rotation trades as easily as crowded continuation tails.
